title: Kabab Koobideh
subtitle: minced lamb kebab
excerpt: Kabab Koobideh is Iran's most famous street food: finely worked minced lamb pressed onto flat wide skewers, grilled over high heat until charred on the outside and juicy inside. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Kabab Koobideh is sold at street stalls and restaurants across Iran and is one of the defining dishes of Persian cuisine. The finely worked mince technique is essential to the texture.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the shaped raw kebabs on a tray, then transfer to a sealed bag. Cook from frozen, adding 3 minutes per side.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Mix and shape the kebabs up to 24 hours ahead. Keep covered in the fridge.

glossaryTerms.definition: From the Persian word for beaten or pounded, describing the finely worked minced meat pressed onto flat skewers to make this classic kebab.
Grilled meat on a skewer, a cornerstone of Persian and Middle Eastern cooking with countless regional variations.

content.text: requires working the mince until it becomes extremely smooth and cohesive. This is what stops the
falling off the skewer during cooking. A food processor achieves the right texture more reliably than mixing by hand. The resting time after shaping is essential. Serves 4.
Use flat metal skewers, not round ones. The flat shape holds the meat in place and allows it to cook evenly on both sides.

items.prepNote: very finely grated, excess liquid squeezed out

content.text: Grate the onion on the fine side of a box grater. Squeeze out as much liquid as possible using a clean cloth or your hands. Excess onion water makes the mix too wet to hold on the skewer.

Place the lamb mince, squeezed onion, parsley, turmeric, cinnamon and allspice in the food processor. Process for 2 to 3 minutes until the mixture is very smooth and almost paste-like. Alternatively, mix by hand for 8 full minutes, kneading with force until cohesive.

Divide the mixture into 8 equal portions. Wet your hands with cold water. Take one portion and press it firmly around a flat skewer, moulding it into a long, flat sausage shape about 2cm thick. Press the edges firmly so there are no air pockets. Repeat with all portions. Refrigerate the shaped skewers for 1 hour.

Heat the cast iron skillet over very high heat until smoking. Brush the kebabs lightly with olive oil. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deeply charred on the outside. Turn only once. Handle gently as the meat is still fragile in the first 2 minutes.
Rest off the heat for 3 minutes. Serve with saffron rice, flatbread, grilled tomatoes and a herb plate of fresh mint and parsley.

attrs.solution: The mixture was not worked long enough or was too wet from onion liquid. Squeeze out every drop of onion water. Process the mince until it becomes completely smooth and sticky. The resting time in the fridge is also essential to firm the mixture.
Use lamb mince with at least 20% fat. Leaner mince dries out fast on a very hot surface. Do not cook beyond 4 minutes per side. The centre should be just cooked through, not overcooked.

attrs.problem: Kebabs are sticking to the pan
attrs.solution: The pan must be smoking hot before the kebabs go in. A cooler pan causes sticking. Leave the kebabs undisturbed for the first 2 minutes. They will release cleanly once a crust has formed.

content.text: Kabab Koobideh is Iran's street food. It is cooked over glowing charcoal in every town and city. The flat skewer shape is Iranian in origin and differs from the round skewer used elsewhere in the Middle East. The combination of allspice, cinnamon and turmeric in the mince is characteristically Persian. It is always served with butter-basted saffron rice and a grilled tomato on the side.
